**CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ - The week April 3rd—10th saw a very large reduction in net long positioning in Nymex platinum contracts. Led by large futures positions, net longs contracted by 180,000 ounces in that period—the largest one-week reduction we have seen since the end of September last year. Tocom positioning also contracted following five consecutive weeks of lengthening. - Palladium futures positions were liquidated as vigorously as those in platinum, with net length on Nymex reduced by more than 180,000 ounces between April 3rd and 10th. Palladium saw a decrease of only 18,000 ounces of open interest however compared with 34,000 ounces in platinum, indicating the entry of more fresh shorts into the market. - After a small rebound last week, net long speculative positioning in silver resumed its six-week downtrend this week with almost 26 million ounces of liquidation. Small speculative futures positions led the way, cutting positions by 15 million ounces. - A fourth consecutive week of ETF liquidation in gold saw 130,000 ounces sold. While most of the major funds we monitor were small sellers, a single European fund accounted for more than 50% of the overall total. - Platinum ETF’s added almost 120,000 ounces to their holdings from January to the beginning of March but have been sellers since then, shedding another 7,800 ounces last week. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **17 April 2012** #### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 #### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 #### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 #### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 #### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **17 April 2012** ## **Gold CFTC data to 10 April 2012; ETF data to 13 April 2012.** ### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

Gold’s $25 bounce to $1,660 on Tuesday 10th was remarkable for its separation from the broader market trend. Risk was sold aggressively, with US equities suffering their worst day year-to-date and growth-focussed assets offered lower throughout the day. Investors flocked instead to Bunds, Treasuries, the US Dollar...and gold. It had been some time since the yellow metal had attracted such seemingly clear-cut ‘safe haven’ bids, giving rise to optimism that its fortunes may be on the turn after a turbulent quarter. Another rally on Thursday propelled prices through $1,660 up to $1,680, but this move occurred on very thin volume and the almost inevitable reversal the following day brought prices to a close just below $1,660. - Net long speculative positioning on Comex declined by 0.7 million ounces to just over 18 million ounces in the week to April 10th. This was a less substantial liquidation than the previous week, which saw net longs cut by 1 million ounces, and may point to a slight improvement in speculators’ sentiment towards gold. The two-month trend of increasing positioning on Tocom remains intact, with another 200,000 ounces added last week. - A fourth consecutive week of ETF liquidation in gold saw 130,000 ounces sold. While most of the major funds we monitor were small sellers, a single European fund accounted for more than 50% of the overall total. ### **Gold Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Apr12** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

- Silver remained true to recent form, imitating and amplifying each move in the gold price last week. After dipping below $31.20 on April 10th, silver benefitted from the ’safe haven’ bids gold received that afternoon to recover to $31.80. The major rally on April 12th saw silver add more than $1, peaking just short of $32.60—this move was a 3.6% gain intraday. Silver made a move of the same magnitude the following day but in the opposite direction, giving up its gains and closing around $0.50 lower on the week. Industrial demand, which has been weak of late, picked up slightly while prices stayed below $32.00 but still remains relatively low. Until this improves, it could hinder any spec-driven rallies that we may see. - After a small rebound last week, net long speculative positioning in silver resumed its six-week downtrend this week with almost 26 million ounces of liquidation. Small speculative futures positions led the way, cutting positions by 15 million ounces. The shortening of net positioning in Comex futures and options is indicative of the general attitude we are currently sensing towards silver at these levels—much of the spec market seems neutral to bearish, with muted industrial demand deterring those on a longer time horizon and silver’s high price volatility discouraging shorter-term investors. - Silver ETF holdings decreased for a second week, with the iSh

ares fund accounting for virtually all the selling. Total holdings across the funds we monitor decreased by 4.3 million ounces and now stand at 456 million ounces. Total holdings have not dipped below 450 million ounces since August 2011. 3 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **17 April 2012** ## **Platinum CFTC data to 10 April 2012; ETF data to 13 April 2012.** # **Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Platinum Investment (oz)** ||**Nymex**

- Platinum lost just over $23 in a choppy week from April 9th—13th. Having traded to $1,630 on the 10th, the ensuing risk selloff sent prices plummeting almost $45 lower. The rally in gold on the same day blew out the spread to $75 in gold’s favour at one point. Prices made a fresh low beneath $1,580 on the 12th but bounced $25 higher along with all the other metals. These gains were erased on Friday the 13th and platinum closed around $1,585—$45 below the week’s high. Fundamental newsflow was thin, and as a result the platinum price mainly washed around with broader macro risk currents. Our Hong Kong office nonetheless reported healthy physical demand in platinum on dips below $1,590, and daily turnover on the Shanghai Gold Exchange continued to increase beyond last month’s average. - The week April 3rd—10th saw a very large reduction in net long positioning in Nymex platinum contracts. Led by large futures positions, net longs contracted by 180,000 ounces in that period—the largest one-week reduction we have seen since

the end of September last year. Tocom positioning also contracted following five consecutive weeks of lengthening. Platinum has suffered more than the other precious metals since the beginning of the new quarter, and these figures show how far investor sentiment had deteriorated in advance of the move below $1,600 on April 10th. Little wonder that the price has found it so hard to recover since then. - Platinum ETF’s added almost 120,000 ounces to their holdings from January to the beginning of March but have been sellers since then, shedding another 7,800 ounces last week. On the daily chart it looks as though palladium may have found its low for the time being with two touches at $630 in the last fortnight. Since then we have seen higher highs and higher lows as the price begins to claw back some ground. $700 remains the key level to regain. - Palladium futures positions were liquidated as vigorously as those in platinum, with net length on Nymex reduced by more than 180,000 ounces between April 3rd and 10th. Palladium saw a decrease of only 18,000 ounces of open interest however compared with 34,000 ounces in platinum, indicating the entry of more fresh shorts into the market. While speculative sentiment has seemed more favourable towards palladium than platinum in recent weeks, these figures suggest an underlying bearishness. - The UK ETFS Palladium fund added 5,000 ounces to its holdings between April 6th—13th.
